card.name: Negation after have/has: yet, not
card.fires_on: The word "yet" or "not" (or n't) right after have, has or had, where a statement says something has not happened. Common in cautionary label statements such as "has not been established".

modes.label: have/has yet to
modes.description: "yet" after have/has/had, followed by "to" and a verb, meaning not done so far.
modes.example: anecdotal accounts of successfully supporting HIV-positive women, the program had<< yet>> to undergo an external evaluation.

modes.label: have/has not (capitalised)
modes.description: "NOT" after HAS/HAVE in all-caps warning text, before "been" and a past participle.

modes.label: lowercase have not / haven't
modes.description: Plain "not" or "'t" after have in ordinary text, saying something has not occurred.
modes.example: If granules have<< not>> dispersed, shake vigorously

card.writes: It adds little clear meaning; the promoted tokens look like Chinese phrases about having heard of or seen something.
card.plain: It marks the spot where a sentence says something has not yet happened or been shown.
